name: Th17 cell
markers: IL-17A, IL-17F and IL-22 (made by the cell)
summary: A helper T cell that defends skin and mucosal surfaces against extracellular bacteria and fungi. Steered by IL-6 and either TGF-β or IL-1β, it makes IL-17 and IL-22, which make epithelial cells produce antimicrobial peptides and neutrophil-calling signals. Too much Th17 activity contributes to autoimmune diseases such as psoriasis.
functions: Develops in the lymph node from a naive CD4 T cell activated by a dendritic cell. In mice IL-6 and TGF-β switch on the transcription factor RORγt; in human cells IL-1β and IL-6 are the key signals.
Debated: the role of TGF-β in human Th17 cells. Some studies find IL-1β and IL-6 enough, others find TGF-β needed alongside them.
Depends on IL-23 from dendritic cells and macrophages to survive, expand and become more inflammatory.

Makes IL-17, which acts on epithelial and stromal cells to produce CXCL8 and G-CSF (calling in neutrophils), and IL-22, which strengthens the epithelial barrier and induces antimicrobial peptides such as defensins.

Defends barriers against extracellular bacteria and fungi such as Candida and Staphylococcus aureus. People who cannot make Th17 cells, through STAT3 mutations, get repeated skin and lung infections with these microbes.
Settles at barrier sites, drawn by CCR6 and the chemokine CCL20 made by epithelial cells. In mice, specific gut bacteria (segmented filamentous bacteria) induce Th17 cells in the gut wall.
Debated: how stable Th17 cells are. In mouse models of inflammation, many convert into Th1-like cells that make IFN-γ, and non-inflammatory and pathogenic Th17 states have been described.
Drives disease when over-active: it is a target in treating psoriasis, where drugs that block IL-17 or IL-23 work well.
abundance: A minority of memory CD4 T cells in human blood (CCR6-positive, CCR4-positive, CXCR3-negative), far more numerous at barrier sites such as the gut wall. In mice, those with normal gut bacteria have many Th17 cells in the small intestine, and germ-free mice have few.
